_comment: Hand-calculated 4-class, 6-query toy problem for exact cosine ranking and the ranking and
classification metrics. Prototypes are one-hot in 4-d, so the cosine score of a query
against class j is exactly the query's j-th coordinate after L2 normalisation, and the
ranking is read off by sorting the coordinates. Query directions are integers; the test
normalises them (normalisation never changes the order, and equal coordinates stay equal).
Expected values below were worked out by hand, not with the code under test.
query  true  direction     coordinates sorted desc  rank order  rank of true  RR   top-1 pred
q5 has an exact tie between b and c (both 3/sqrt(23)); the tie rule orders them by
class id, b before c, so exactly one query is tied.
Ranking metrics: ranks [1,1,1,3,3,4]; Top-1 3/6 = 0.5; Top-2 0.5; Top-3 5/6; Top-4 and
median rank (1+3)/2 = 2; percentiles by linear interpolation over sorted [1,1,1,3,3,4]:
normalised rank (rank-1)/(C-1) = [0,0,0,2/3,2/3,1], mean 7/18.
Classification from top-1 predictions [a,b,c,a,b,c] vs true [a,b,c,d,a,b]:
class  TP FP FN  P    R    F1     support
d      0  0  1   0    0    0      1   (never predicted: zero_division=0, affected count 1)
accuracy 3/6; macro P 3/8, R 1/2, F1 5/12; weighted P 5/12, R 1/2, F1 4/9;
balanced accuracy = macro recall = 1/2.
